3.2. DeepReach and an Iterative Scenario-Based Probabilistic Safety Verification Method
Instead of solving the HJB-VI over a grid, DeepReach (Bansal and Tomlin, 2021) learns a param-
eterized approximation of the value function using a sinusoidal deep neural network (DNN). Thus,
memory and complexity requirements for training scale with the value function complexity rather
than the grid resolution, allowing it to obtain BRTs for high-dimensional systems. DeepReach trains
the DNN via self-supervision on the HJB-VI itself. Ultimately, it takes as input a state x and time
t, and it outputs a learned value function ˜V (x, t). ˜V (x, t) also induces a corresponding safe policy
˜π(x, t), as well as a BRT (referred to as the neural reachable tube from hereon).
However, the neural reachable tube will only be as accurate as ˜V (x, t). To obtain a prov-
ably safe BRT, Lin and Bansal (2023) propose a uniform value correction bound which is defined,
for the avoid case, as the maximum learned value of an unsafe state under the induced policy:
δ ˜V ,˜π := maxx∈X{ ˜V (x, 0) : J˜π(x, 0) ≤0}. The authors show that the super-δ ˜V ,˜π level set of
˜V (x, 0) is provably safe under the policy ˜π(x, t). They also propose an iterative scenario-based
probabilistic verification method for computing an approximation of δ ˜V ,˜π from finite random sam-
ples that satisfies a desired confidence level and violation rate. However, the method is sensitive to
outlier errors in the neural reachable tube and can result in very conservative safe sets. Specifically,
it does not provide safety assurances for safe sets with nonzero empirical safety violations.
In this work, we propose probabilistic safety verification methods that allow nonzero empirical
safety violations at the cost of the probabilistic strength of safety. This enables a direct trade-off
between resilience to outlier errors and the strength of the safety guarantee.
Remark 1 Although we work with DeepReach solutions in particular for our problem setup, our
proposed approaches can verify any general ˜V (x, t) and ˜π(x, t), regardless of whether DeepReach,
a numerical PDE solver, or some other tool is used to obtain them.

## **3.2. DeepReach and an Iterative Scenario-Based Probabilistic Safety Verification Method** 

Instead of solving the HJB-VI over a grid, DeepReach (Bansal and Tomlin, 2021) learns a parameterized approximation of the value function using a sinusoidal deep neural network (DNN). Thus, memory and complexity requirements for training scale with the value function complexity rather than the grid resolution, allowing it to obtain BRTs for high-dimensional systems. DeepReach trains the DNN via self-supervision on the HJB-VI itself. They also propose an iterative scenario-based probabilistic verification method for computing an approximation of _δ_ ˜ _V ,π_ ˜ from finite random samples that satisfies a desired confidence level and violation rate.
